Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

3.5 The illustrations are diagrammatic only and are not intended to illustrate the details of design. 

3.6 Toferances on untoleranced dimensions shall be in accordance with the best prevalent practice. 

4. Material — Suitable material used for various components shall be as given below and shall fulfill 
the requirements laid down in 5 and 6: 



Components 
Jaw sleeve, body and handle 

Jaw 



Material 

C15 of Schedule II of IS : 1570-1961 ' Schedules for wrought 
steels for general engineering purposes ' 

T50 of Schedule VI of 15:1570-1961 with a maximum 
sulphur and phosphorus content of 0'05 percent each 



5. Hardness — Hardness for jaws shall be 400 to 500 H/ ( ;=J 41 to 49 HRC ). 

6. Manufacturoi Workmanship and Tinish — The threads In the jaw sleeves and the body shall be 
accurately cut. The jaw sleeve, body and handle shall be properly knurled. The jaws shall be 
properly machined and the segments accurately and urriformiy cut. The handle and the jaw shall be 
drive fit to the body. The vices shall be free from cracks, seams, burrs and other defects. All 
sharp corners and edges except the knurled portions shall be removed. Threads shall be full and 
irue. The jaw sleeve shall move freely and evenly in the body without any undue play or stiffness. 
The segments of the jaws shall meet evenly and simultaneously and the aperture in between shall be 
truly concentric at any point of operation. The pin vices shall be finished smooth and shall have 
suitable nickel chromium plating according to IS : 1068-1968 * Specification for electroplated coatings 
of nickel and chromium on iron and steel '- 

7. Tests 

7.i Performance Test — The pin vices shall be capable of firmly gripping maximum and minimum 
size of mild steel wire as given below: 



Nominal Size 

1 

2 
3 
4

Min 
0*2 
0-8

2-8

1-0

18:8177-1976 

The wires so held shall not slip out of the jaws on normal pull by hand and rotate in between 
Ihe jaws when reasonably twisted with pliers at a point not exceexJing 25 mm from the end of 
the jaw. 

7-2 Adhesion Tesf — When rubbed with the back of the l<nife blade 10 to 15 times, the nickel plating 
shall not be peeled off and shall not show any sign of damage. 

4. Marking — The pin vices shall be clearly and legibly stamped with the nominal size, manufacturer's 
.name, initials and the recognized trade-mark. The year of manufacture shall also be marked legibly 
if required by the purchaser. 

9A ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard deals with the pin vices used by instrument makers for firmly holding small 
diameter pins, wires and small diameter rods which are being filed, threaded or\ground. While 
preparing this standard assistance has beenAerlved from Drawing No. IND/GS/2057 'Vices, pin, 
chuck type' issued by thef Chief Inspectorate V€eneral Stores, Ka/ipUr.
